items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I was not that great at transcribing when it would be like Schoenberg’s F# minor string quartet, stuff like that.

ctx.x: Did you get a reputation in the studio for a certain style?

I was a versatile guy. I mean if they needed a banjo I’d go and borrow a banjo for the session. But because I understood the nature of the versatility. Now as a teenager I was playing with rock bands as well as doing the money stuff. And I mean making five pounds for a gig was a lot better than babysitting or washing my neighbor’s car, although if I washed my neighbor’s car I got tickets for Tottenham Hotspur’s games, which was the local soccer team. So it was worth it. But I was doing a lot of stuff. I mean as…

stepchild of that whole world. And still to this day it’s somewhat that way. So when I got better grades than I expected I said wait a minute, why am I going to leave London? I grew up in London and I’d been paying my dues as a teenager and getting demo sessions and playing with all these cats, why do I want to leave all that? So I canceled my application to Leeds, took a gap year — I was a pioneer of the gap year. I mean this was like 1971. And I applied to Goldsmith’s College, London University, which was the…
